subject: Split KMS escrow & network design — handoff and rotation controls
messages:
From: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@acme-corp.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Splitting KMS custody for private deployment (initial ask)

Marcus —

Thanks for taking the call last week. As mentioned, Acme is moving forward with a private VPC deployment of Redwood Inference in our AWS account. Two items we need your help designing:

1) We need a key custody model that supports split control (no single human or service can unilaterally access customer master keys). Ideally we would integrate our HSM-backed KMS (CloudVault) for BYOK, but we also want an escrow option for emergency recovery that satisfies our auditors.

2) Network topology and connector requirements for HSM/KMS access from Redwood's on-prem connector (we're planning a VPC peering + private link fallback).

Attached a high-level network diagram and a short list of compliance questions from our security team. High priority: rotation cadence, audit log retention, and proof-of-escrow controls.

Can you share a proposed operational pattern (how keys are provisioned, what stops automated rotation, who signs off for emergency un-escrow) and a short checklist of firewall rules / ports for our infra team?

Thanks — Tom

[Attachment: network-diagram.pdf (diagram)]

--
Tom Reeves
Head of Platform, Acme Corp

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@acme-corp.com>
Cc: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Splitting KMS custody for private deployment (initial ask)

Tom —

Appreciate the diagram and the clear list of asks. Drafting a proposed pattern here to get alignment before a short design review:

High-level proposal:
- BYOK + HSM-backed customer KMS: Acme generates/imports the customer master key (CMK) into CloudVault HSM. Redwood never persistently holds the CMK material.
- Envelope encryption: Redwood uses a short-lived service envelope key (SEK) per deployment generated by Redwood's runtime. The SEK is wrapped/unwrapped by Acme's CMK via KMS API calls over a mutual-TLS channel.
- Split-escrow for recovery: an escrow key is created within a separate CloudVault key account under a multi-party governance policy (two independent approvers). Escrow material is stored encrypted in the customer-controlled S3 bucket. Redwood's runtime is configured to call the escrow unwrap only if both escrow approvers approve via a recorded DocuSign workflow.
- Rotation: CMK rotation remains controlled by Acme; SEK rotation is automated every 24 hours by default, configurable to 6–72 hours depending on latency/cost. All rotations are logged and immutably audited.

Network and connector notes (short checklist):
- Primary: VPC Peering between Acme and Redwood Dedicated VPCs.
- Fallback: AWS PrivateLink endpoint for KMS API traffic from Redwood runtime to Acme KMS (regionally bound).
- mTLS: mandatory for KMS proxy calls; Redwood will provide client certs issued by Acme's CA.
- Ports: allow outbound 443 from Redwood connectors to Acme KMS endpoint; allow inbound from Redwood connector IPs if you host an on-prem KMS proxy.
- Firewall: allow NAT for connector to reach CloudVault; restrict CIDR to Redwood connector/egress IPs.

Audit, governance, and controls:
- Immutable key usage logs forwarded to Acme's Central Audit S3 bucket (retention configurable).
- Rotation alerts and regression checks routed to both Acme SecOps and Redwood SRE.
- Emergency escrow unwrapping requires a DocuSign-signed request and two internal approvers; the unwrapping call is rate-limited and fully logged.

Attachments: I attached a KMS handoff checklist that maps owners and approvals for each step. Can we set up a 45-minute design review early next week? I'll have Mina there to cover network and runtime constraints and Laura to cover HSM compliance patterns.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: kms-handoff-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Splitting KMS custody for private deployment (initial ask)

Marcus —

Quick internal notes to prepare for the review with Acme:

On the envelope model: good call. Implementation details to confirm:
- KMS calls must be synchronous for unwrap during cold start; ensure a short retry/backoff strategy to avoid startup cascades.
- For split custody, recommend using CloudVault's "dual-approval" HSM key policy paired with an external approval service (DocuSign or internal ticketing that calls CloudVault's approve API).

Network considerations (detailed):
- If Acme prefers VPC peering: ensure route table entries do not inadvertently expose management ports (22, 2379). We should only allow app-plane traffic and KMS-port 443 (API) to CloudVault.
- PrivateLink option: advise using PrivateLink for KMS API; PrivateLink keeps traffic on the AWS backbone and is simpler for security reviews. We'll need to supply the PrivateLink service name and approved subnets.
- For on-prem HSMs behind NAT: require a reverse proxy inside the customer DMZ that validates client certs and proxies to the HSM. Redwood will trust only the client cert chain anchored at Acme's CA.

Operational constraints and telemetry:
- Rotation automation: use CloudVault key-versioning and tag each SEK unwrap/rewrap call with deployment-id and node-id. Persist the event stream to an S3 audit bucket and replicate to Acme's SIEM via Kinesis or partner connector.
- Retention: auditors usually ask for 7 years for critical key events; we should surface this as a configurable field in the deployment template.

Action items for the review:
- Marcus: present the envelope flow and the DocuSign escrow flow.
- Laura: bring prior HSM policy examples and any SOC2 references.
- Dylan: confirm Runtime fallback behavior (how we fall back from CMK unwrap failure to cached prefixes).

Also flagged: we need a short DocuSign template for the escrow approval workflow; Legal should weigh in but for the review we can show a mockup.

Thanks — Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
